title: library-article (_library/<topic>/<article>.md) runtime body-structure + size contract
description: Hook-and-scan-consumable runtime artifact for durable universal-knowledge library articles at _library/<topic>/<article>.md — one concept per file, synthesized by the librarian at promotion and scrubbed of all plan/project-specific detail. The k8s ValidatingAdmissionPolicy paramKind for the library-article type. This contract is the canonical home for the article's size_limits and the routing activation-condition field that the library-index scan reads as the first source for index Description columns. The frontmatter type registration (type: reference) lives in governance/frontmatter-rules.json#types.reference; this contract carries the WHAT-it-contains body-structure and the length governance.

_design_notes.consumer: skills/librarian/capabilities/library-scrub.sh emits the article at promotion (synthesizes the routing one-liner + scrubbed body); skills/librarian/capabilities/library-index.sh reads size_limits at the audit-time re-derive scan to emit the over-threshold finding and consumes routing as the first Description-derivation source. The templates/library-article.md scaffold instantiates this contract.
_design_notes.evolution_protocol: R-37 atomic lockstep — this runtime artifact + governance/frontmatter-rules.json#types.reference (the type registration) + the hook SCHEMA_KEY dispatch + governance/foundation-master.json forward-composed move in one commit.
_design_notes.type_registration_rationale: The article type is registered via the frontmatter pillar, not the tagging pillar; frontmatter is the activation surface the index generators read to route a reader to the article.

routing.description: Activation-condition one-liner ('when to read this'): a precise scope/applicability statement synthesized at promotion. The FIRST source the index Description-derivation chain reads, ahead of description / H1 / first-paragraph.
routing.routing_rationale: A net-new activation-condition field, carried by no other shipped contract; it lets an index row state when a reader should open the article rather than restating its title, which is what makes a coverage signal load-bearing at research time.

revalidation_interval_days.guidance: Per-article staleness-velocity tier. Fast-moving tool documentation revalidates near 45 days; stable concepts near 270; the freshness scan applies a 90-day fallback when the field is undeclared.
revalidation_interval_days.revalidation_interval_days_rationale: Different knowledge ages at different rates, so a single global staleness window either nags on durable concepts or lets fast-moving tool docs rot; a per-article tier with a safe default keeps the freshness signal trustworthy.

size_limits.enforcement_detail: Length is enforced by the librarian library-index re-derive scan, which emits an over-threshold finding when an article exceeds the soft budget — NEVER by a write-time guard. No write-time body-structure or line-count guard governs library articles in the runtime.
size_limits.split_vs_pointer_rule: An article over the soft budget that is MECE-decomposable is split into per-sub-topic articles; one over the soft budget that is a single-topic narrative gains an in-doc table of contents above the body (never auto-generated).
size_limits.size_limits_rationale: A soft budget keeps each article one readable concept and an audit-time scan flags overflow without a write-time block, so a long synthesis is never silently truncated and the author decides between splitting and adding a manual table of contents.

h1.match_rule: the H1 is the concept name (one concept per file)
h1.rationale: The single top-level heading names the durable concept the article carries; bare-wikilink cross-references resolve against the basename, which mirrors this concept name.

leading_section_index.rationale: A leading in-document section index is forbidden; the article is short enough that a reader scans the body directly, and an auto-generated index drifts from hand-edited prose.

in_document_toc.rationale: An in-doc table of contents is permitted only when the article exceeds the soft budget and is not decomposable, and it is authored by hand, never auto-generated.

sibling_wikilinks_at_foot.placement: at the foot of the body
sibling_wikilinks_at_foot.rationale: Sibling articles are cross-referenced with bare wikilinks at the foot for backlink-graph value; basename uniqueness backs the bare form, and the basename-collision scan guards it.

synthesized_body.rationale: The body is synthesized at promotion and scrubbed of all plan/project-specific detail (task IDs, plan slugs, engagement names, decision dates); it is regenerated content, not hand-maintained prose, so per-article changelogs are replaced by the single global library log.
